bib.title: MM1: Methods, Analysis & Insights from Multimodal LLM Pre-training

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; qualitative example figures (App. D, Figs 11-17) read only as text fragments.

question: Which choices of image encoder, vision-language connector and pre-training data mixture matter most when building a performant multimodal LLM?
contributions: Small-scale ablations over model architecture (image encoder, resolution, VL connector) and pre-training data (caption, interleaved, text-only, synthetic).
Design lessons from those ablations, shown to transfer to SFT.
MM1 family: dense 3B, 7B, 30B and MoE 3B (64 experts, 64B total) and 7B (32 experts, 47B total), SOTA on few-shot pre-training metrics and competitive after SFT on 12 benchmarks.

method.summary: Ablate one component at a time on a 1.2B-LLM base (ViT-L/14 CLIP encoder, C-Abstractor with 144 tokens, 45/45/10 caption/interleaved/text mix), then scale the chosen recipe (ViT-H 378px CLIP, C-Abstractor 144 tokens) to 3B/7B/30B dense and MoE LLMs, pre-train 200k steps unfrozen, and SFT on 1.45M examples with high-resolution support.
method.task: multimodal LLM pre-training (image-text to text) and supervised fine-tuning for VQA, captioning and MLLM benchmarks

datasets.name: Captioned images (CC3M, CC12M, HQIPT-204M, COYO, Web Image-Text-1B internal)
datasets.preprocessing: image-text pairs packed along sequence; attention masks block cross-example attention

datasets.name: Synthetic captions VeCap-300M
datasets.split: part of caption data (about 7% of caption data)

datasets.name: Interleaved image-text (OBELICS, Web Interleaved internal)
datasets.size: 600M documents (Table 2); App. A.1 says internal set is 500M documents, 1B images, 500B text tokens
datasets.preprocessing: drop documents with no images or more than 30; filter images (corrupt, aspect ratio <1/2 or >2, <100px or >10,000px, URL containing logo/button/icon/plugin/widget); dedupe images whose URL or MD5 appeared more than 10 times; keep first occurrence per page

datasets.name: Text-only (webpages, code, social media, books, encyclopedic, math)
datasets.source: 150B English HTML files filtered to 3B; boilerplate removal, GPT-3/CCNet-style quality filters, exact-hash and LSH dedup

datasets.name: SFT mixture (LLaVA-Conv 57k, LLaVA-Complex 77k, ShareGPT-4V 102k, VQAv2 83k, GQA 72k, OKVQA 9k, OCRVQA 80k, DVQA 200k, ChartQA 18k, AI2D 3k, DocVQA 39k, InfoVQA 24k, A-OKVQA 66k, COCO Captions 83k, TextCaps 22k, SynthDog-EN 500k, text-only 13k)
datasets.preprocessing: academic sets formatted as instructions per LLaVA-1.5, e.g. 'Answer the question using a single word or phrase.'

datasets.name: Pre-training eval: COCO, NoCaps, TextCaps, VQAv2, TextVQA, VizWiz, OKVQA
datasets.split: COCO Karpathy test; NoCaps val; TextCaps val; VQAv2 testdev; TextVQA val; VizWiz testdev; OKVQA val (ablations use val splits for VQAv2 and VizWiz)

datasets.name: SFT eval: VQAv2, TextVQA, ScienceQA-IMG, MMMU, MathVista, MME, MMBench, SEED-Bench, POPE, LLaVA-Bench-in-the-Wild, MM-Vet

models.name: MM1 ablation base
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer LLM + ViT-L/14 CLIP (DFN-5B + VeCap-300M, 336x336) + C-Abstractor, 144 image tokens

models.name: MM1-3B / MM1-7B / MM1-30B
models.architecture: ViT-H 378x378 CLIP (DFN-5B) + C-Abstractor 144 tokens + decoder-only LLM
models.init_from: image encoder and LLM decoder both initialised from in-house pre-trained models; LLM pre-trained on the text-only mixture
models.context: 4096 tokens, up to 16 images per sequence

models.name: MM1-3B-MoE / MM1-7B-MoE
models.params: 64B total (3B-MoE, 64 experts, sparse layer every 2 layers); 47B total (7B-MoE, 32 experts, sparse layer every 4 layers)
models.architecture: GShard/ST-MoE style, top-2 gating, load-balance loss 0.01, router z-loss 0.001; only decoder replaced

models.name: Flamingo, IDEFICS, Emu2, LLaVA-NeXT, CogVLM, Gemini, GPT-4V etc.

training.objective: inferred: next-token (autoregressive) text prediction on image-text sequences; paper does not name the loss
training.optimizer: AdamW (decoupled weight decay), gradient clip max norm 1; SFT uses AdaFactor
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay to 10% of peak over 2e5 steps (pre-training); cosine decay to 0 (SFT)
training.seq_len: 4096 (pre-training, up to 16 images at 378x378, 144 tokens each); 2048 (SFT)
training.seeds: mixing done once offline into a fixed deterministic snapshot; all models see same examples in same order; different input-pipeline seeds had non-negligible impact

other.unfrozen: all models pre-trained entirely unfrozen; SFT keeps encoder and LLM unfrozen
other.lr_fit: eta = exp(-0.4214 ln(N) - 0.5535), N non-embedding params; grid on 9M, 85M, 302M, 1.2B; fit on 8-shot average; predicted 2.2e-5 for N=3e10
other.batch composition: roughly 1M text tokens and 1M image tokens per batch
other.high resolution SFT: positional embedding interpolation to 448, 560, 672 px (672 px = 2,304 tokens); sub-image decomposition: 672x672 downsampled global image plus 4 sub-images of 1344 resized image, up to 1792x1792; default for Table 4 is 1344x1344 with 720 tokens per image

inference.decoding: greedy decoding until EOS or stop tokens (newline for captioning; '.', ',', 'Question' also for VQA)
inference.samples: few-shot prompts randomly sampled per dataset from train (else val) set, query excluded; GPT-4-judged benchmarks (MM-Vet, LLaVA-Bench) run 3 times and averaged
inference.prompting: pre-training eval: '{IMAGE} A photo of' for captioning, '{IMAGE} Question: {QUESTION} Short answer:' for VQA; 0/4/8/16-shot; MM1-30B-Chat MathVista with few-shot chain-of-thought

parameters.mixed-resolution in-context examples: only last N=3 images use sub-image decomposition, earlier in-context examples low resolution; enables 8-shot

metrics.name: SFT meta-average
metrics.definition: each benchmark divided by the baseline config (224px, attention pooling, 64 queries), then averaged; baseline = 100

eval.protocol: ablations: zero-shot and 4/8-shot averages over captioning and VQA tasks; single runs, no significance tests stated; only larger baselines compared in pre-training table

availability.code: AXLearn framework (github.com/apple/axlearn); no MM1 training code stated
availability.data: includes internal datasets (Web Image-Text-1B, Web Interleaved, text-only, SFT text-only) not released

evidence.quote: we used η equal to 6e-5, 4e-5, and 2e-5, respectively

results.claim: Raising image resolution from 224 to 336 gives roughly a 3% boost on all ablation metrics across encoders, the largest single encoder effect.
results.quote: increasing image resolution from 224 to 336 results in approx. 3% boost in all metrics across all architectures

results.claim: Doubling encoder size ViT-L to ViT-H gives a modest gain, usually under 1%.
results.quote: a doubling in parameters, results in a modest performance increase of usually less than 1%

results.claim: Adding VeCap-300M synthetic captions to encoder pre-training gives more than 1% few-shot boost.
results.quote: yields more than 1% boost in few-shot scenarios

results.claim: Contrastive ViT-L encoders beat the reconstructive AIM600M of comparable size by 0.3 to 1.5%; AIM was trained on under half the data so the result is inconclusive.
results.quote: result in 0.3% to 1.5% performance gain compared to AIM600M of comparable size

results.claim: Number of visual tokens and image resolution matter most; the VL connector type has little effect.
results.setup: Fig. 4, 1.2B LLM, avg pooling vs attention pooling vs C-Abstractor, 224/336px, 64/144 tokens
results.quote: Number of visual tokens and image resolution matters most, while the type of VL connector has little effect.
results.note: Contradicts Honeybee's reported gains for C-Abstractor.

results.claim: Zero-shot score rises from 25.8 to 39.3 as caption share increases, while at least 50% interleaved data is needed to keep 8-shot above 61.
results.setup: 1.2B base, 200k steps, caption/interleaved mixing ratios, Fig 5a
results.quote: Zero-shot performance increases consistently, from 25.8% to 39.3%

results.claim: Without interleaved data, 8-shot and 4-shot performance drop to 45% and 43.7%.
results.quote: Without it, performance drops drastically to 45% and 43.7%, respectively.

results.claim: A caption/interleaved/text ratio of 5:5:1 balances multimodal and text-only performance.
results.quote: with caption/interleaved/text ratio 5:5:1, we achieve a good balance

results.claim: Synthetic VeCap captions (7% of caption data) add 2.4% and 4% absolute in few-shot.
results.quote: it does give a non-trivial boost in few-shot performance, of 2.4% and 4% absolute

results.claim: MM1-30B 8-shot COCO CIDEr beats Flamingo-80B and IDEFICS-80B.
results.setup: Table 3, MM1-30B vs IDEFICS-80B (114.3, includes COCO in training) and Flamingo-80B (108.8)
results.table: Table 3, row MM1-30B, shot 8, column COCO

results.claim: MM1-30B 8-shot VQAv2 70.9 vs Emu2-37B 67.8 and Flamingo-80B 65.6.
results.table: Table 3, row MM1-30B, shot 8, column VQAv2

results.claim: MM1 outperforms all published prior pre-trained MLLMs in few-shot.
results.setup: Table 3; only compared with larger models; comparable to Emu2 on VQAv2, TextVQA, OKVQA at 30B
results.quote: MM1 outperforms all published prior work for pre-trained MLLMs.

results.claim: Optimal peak LR fit predicts 2.2e-5 for 30B.
results.setup: log-linear fit on 9M-1.2B grid searches using 8-shot average; validation loss not correlated with downstream performance
results.quote: For N = 3e10, this fit predicts η = 2.2e−5

results.claim: MM1-30B-Chat scores 73.5 on TextVQA and 1637.6 on MME perception, beating LLaVA-NeXT-34B on TextVQA (69.5) and Emu2-Chat-37B (66.6).
MM1-30B-Chat MMMU val 44.7 vs LLaVA-NeXT-34B 51.1 and GPT4V 56.8: still behind on MMMU and MM-Vet (48.7 vs 57.4).
Supporting 1344x1344 resolution gives a 15% relative increase in SFT meta-average over a 336px baseline; 1792x1792 slightly decreases.
results.setup: Fig 7b, MM1-3B, positional interpolation plus sub-image decomposition
results.quote: we can achieve a 15% relative increase by supporting an image resolution of 1344×1344

results.claim: MM1-30B-Chat MathVista with chain-of-thought: 4-shot 41.9 vs zero-shot 39.4, 8-shot with mixed-resolution examples 44.4, despite only single-image SFT data.
results.setup: MM1-30B-Chat, 8 in-context examples, only last N=3 at high resolution
results.quote: Using this formulation with 8 in-context examples increases the performance on MathVista to 44.4.

results.claim: MM1 uses 720 image tokens in total versus 2,880 per image for LLaVA-NeXT, enabling multi-image and few-shot prompting.
results.setup: MM1-30B-Chat at 1344px with 5 sub-images x 144 tokens
results.quote: each image is represented as 2,880 tokens sent to the LLM, while ours is only 720 in total
results.note: App. C.5 describes 2,880 tokens for 20 effective images (4-shot x 5 sub-images x 144) rather than per image; the main text attributes 2,880 per image to LLaVA-NeXT.

results.claim: When SFT-ing at low resolution a frozen encoder is better (+2.2 points); at 1344px unfreezing is better (+2.9 points).
results.quote: it is beneficial to unfreeze the image encoder (+2.9 points)

results.claim: MoE variants beat their dense counterparts on almost every SFT benchmark.
results.setup: Table 4, 3B-MoE (64 experts) and 7B-MoE (32 experts) vs dense
results.quote: Our MoE models achieve uniformly better performance

limits: Ablations run at 1.2B (2.9B for encoders) scale and extrapolated to 30B; no confirmation of lessons at 30B for each choice.
No seeds or variance reported; authors note input-pipeline seeds changed results non-negligibly, and fixed one data order.
Hardware, compute and wall-clock not stated; internal data and weights not released.
Encoder comparison between AIM and CLIP is inconclusive because AIM saw under half the data.
Zero-shot results are not hill-climbed since they reflect prompt-format fit; SFT benchmarks measure mostly zero-shot, single-image.
MM1-30B-Chat trails LLaVA-NeXT-34B on MMMU and MM-Vet and GPT-4V/Gemini on several benchmarks (Table 4).
Resolution beyond 1344 (1792) slightly lowers average, attributed to resizing artifacts (unverified).
Pre-training table compares only against larger published models; IDEFICS includes COCO in training.
